question: Should OpenClaw support the public `api.registerReadinessCriterion` plugin API and operator-selected `gateway.readiness` criteria as a maintained v1 compatibility contract?
rationale: The branch turns plugin callbacks and configuration identifiers into externally usable product surface; tests can validate mechanics but cannot determine whether OpenClaw should permanently own that API and operational semantics.

options.title: Approve the v1 readiness contract
options.body: Accept the public plugin criterion API and operator-selected readiness configuration, then require exact-head live compatibility and recovery proof before landing this follow-on.

options.title: Ship core observations without plugin registration
options.body: Defer the public plugin API and keep only core-owned readiness observations until a later plugin-contract decision.

options.title: Pause the readiness stack
options.body: Defer both the parent framework and owner-adoption work until hosting-readiness direction is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Approve the v1 readiness contract
recommendation.body: Accept the public plugin criterion API and operator-selected readiness configuration, then require exact-head live compatibility and recovery proof before landing this follow-on.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the linked parent readiness proposal and can incorporate maintainer direction into the stacked series; final acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
